thread:
maria.customer: seeing intermittent 401s in the Console when trying to save project settings. Happens in both Chrome and Safari. No repro from curl yet.

alex.support: thanks — sorry about that. can you grab a HAR + console logs and paste the x-request-id from the failing response headers? that will let us trace the backend. also share the account id and approximate times.

maria.customer: account id: acct_7G2... happened ~2026-03-17T14:12-14:16 UTC. attaching screenshot next.

alex.support: perfect. steps to capture (Chrome):
1) Open Chrome -> Menu -> More tools -> Developer tools (or `Ctrl+Shift+I`).
2) Network tab: check "Preserve log" and "Disable cache".
3) Console tab: right-click -> "Save as..." to export console logs (or select all text and copy).
4) Reproduce the issue.
5) Network tab: right-click any request -> "Save all as HAR with content" (this includes response bodies).
6) For the failing request, right-click -> "Copy" -> "Copy as cURL" and paste here. We need the full headers (particularly `Authorization` removed) and the response headers which contain `x-request-id`.

alex.support: Safari (Web Inspector) quick steps:
1) Safari -> Preferences -> Advanced -> enable "Show Develop menu".
2) Develop -> Show Web Inspector -> Network tab.
3) Check "Preserve Log" if present, reproduce, then click the export icon at bottom-right to save a .har.
4) Console tab -> select -> Save as...

chris.sre: quick curl tips to capture response headers (so you can paste request id):
- Use `-i` to include response headers or `-D -` to dump headers to stdout. e.g.
```
curl -i -X POST "https://api.redwood.inference/v1/responses"
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REPLACE_WITH_TOKEN"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```
Look for `x-request-id` or `x-rdin-request-id` in the response header. If you see a long hex string, paste it here.

maria.customer: attaching HAR and console.txt now. also pasted the cURL I copied from Chrome (sanitized):
```
# copied-as-curl from browser
curl 'https://api.redwood.inference/v1/responses'
  -H 'authority: api.redwood.inference'
  -H 'authorization: Bearer <TOKEN_REDACTED>'
  -H 'content-type: application/json'
  --data-raw '{"input":"save settings"}'
  --compressed
```
response showed a 401 and headers: `x-request-id: 0a1b2c3d-4e5f-6a7b-8c9d-0123456789ab`

alex.support: got it — thanks. can you also tell us whether this happens only after being idle? any proxy/VPN?

maria.customer: only after long idle (browser open overnight). no VPN.

chris.sre: likely stale auth tokens or a rotating key. next steps from our side:
- we'll search logs for `0a1b2c3d-4e5f-6a7b-8c9d-0123456789ab` and correlate with auth service traces.
- if we can reproduce, we may ask you to run the same cURL but with `-v` and `-i` so we can see WWW-Authenticate headers.

alex.support: one more upload request — when you attach the HAR and console bundle to the support ticket, please include: account id, page URL (exact), local time, steps to reproduce (idle -> click save), and the cURL you pasted. if you can also repro in Incognito and attach that HAR, it helps rule out extension interference.

maria.customer: uploading to ticket now (files: screenshot.png, settings-save.har, console-log.txt, copied-curl.txt).

upload-bot: debug-bundle received and attached to ticket #12345 by maria.customer (settings-save.har, console-log.txt).

alex.support: thank you — I've escalated to SRE with the request id and the HAR. we'll update once we have a root cause. :thumbsup:
